title: ANDS Studio — The whole product, end to end
walkthrough:
Every authenticated page carries a persistent amber banner at the top: "Demo / evaluation environment — nothing here is transmitted to Health Canada and no email is sent. Use it to explore the full workflow safely."

The first screen is a sign-in card branded "ANDS Studio" with an EN / FR language toggle in its top corner. Its heading is "Sign in," with the line "Your clients' dossiers are isolated per workspace." and a maple-leaf residency note "Self-hosted: run ANDS Studio in your own environment so your data can stay resident in Canada." There are Email and Password fields and a "Sign in →" button, disabled until both are filled. A secondary button reads "New here? Create a workspace"; switching shows the heading "Create your workspace" and a "Who are you filing for?" choice — "Your own company" or "On behalf of clients (CRO)" — which changes the copy: the own-company note is "One workspace for your company — dossiers, documents and filings stay isolated to your organisation," and the CRO note is "One workspace per client company — dossiers, documents and filings stay isolated between the clients you file for." The company field is labeled "Your company name" (placeholder "Acme Therapeutics Inc.") or "Client company name" (placeholder "Northbridge Regulatory CRO") depending on that choice, and a live password check shows "At least 10 characters, with letters and numbers." then "✓ Meets the password rules." A "Forgot password?" flow issues a one-time code; in this environment a notice states "Demo environment — no outbound email. In a production deployment this code is emailed to [your address] and never displayed. Here it is available on-screen, but hidden until you reveal it so it is never accidentally captured in a screenshot of a real workflow." — the code stays hidden behind a "Reveal demo code" button, and the code field is labeled "One-time code" (placeholder "8-digit code"). The sign-in card also offers a "Sign in with your organization (SSO) →" option (OpenID Connect, per-workspace). If an account has MFA, an "Authenticator code" field appears with "This account has multi-factor authentication enabled — a second code from your phone. Enter the current 6-digit code from your authenticator app."

The home page headline reads "File your ANDS with Health Canada — guided end to end." with a paragraph explaining an Abbreviated New Drug Submission "walks you through it step by step — every term explained in plain language." The button is "Start my submission →". Below it an "Other ways to start" card carries chips "Managing several products? Open the dossier catalog →" and "Portfolio roll-up →" (each showing a live count when there are dossiers), plus a note that bilingual Module 1 and the Product Monograph (EN + FR) status live inside each dossier. A persistent "Trust & security" strip sits above the footer, with chips "Canada," "Isolation," "Roles," "Audit" and "SOC 2 / SSO · roadmap," and a "One-page security summary" expander that plainly states what is live (self-hosted Canadian residency, per-workspace tenant isolation refused at the API, roles / segregation of duties, append-only actor+UTC-stamped exportable audit trail) versus roadmap (SOC 2, SSO/SAML, SCIM). The footer line reads "Grounded in real Health Canada process · your progress is saved automatically." Once started, a step rail, a step card, a "Submission Tower" of module tiles, and a readiness panel appear; the top bar shows either "Ready to file" or a percentage chip like "72% ready," and a "Reset session" button (which opens a typed-confirmation modal — you type RESET — noting the dossier and its append-only audit trail remain saved server-side and re-openable, so a reset only detaches the local session). Navigation chips across all pages link Journey, Dossiers, Portfolio, Registry, Correspondence, and Help.

"Your product dossiers" is the dossier manager. Text explains a Dossier ID "is the permanent file for one product at Health Canada" and that "client workspaces are isolated end-to-end (per-workspace data partitions, tenant-checked on every request, cross-client access is structurally impossible)." "New dossier +" opens a form with Dossier ID (placeholder "e123456") and Product name (placeholder "Drugazole 10 mg tablet"), plus a Submission type selector (ANDS / SANDS / SNDS) and optional Client / sponsor and Owner (PM) fields; invalid IDs show "Dossier ID must be one letter + 6–7 digits (e.g. e123456)." A note says Health Canada issues the Dossier ID when you file a Dossier ID Request through REP (via your CESG account), with "No ID yet? Start with a placeholder →". Placeholder (draft) dossiers carry a "⚠ placeholder — set real ID ✎" chip; clicking opens a "Set the real Health Canada Dossier ID" modal that re-keys the dossier to the ID issued by Health Canada, noting "All documents, sequences and history move with it, and export unblocks once a real ID is set." Each tile shows a progress bar and a modules-built count like "3/9 modules built" — or, when all required modules are built, "3/9 modules built — validate to file" (structural completeness is explicitly not a filing verdict; a real eCTD validation pass is still required). Deleting opens a "Delete this dossier?" modal that requires typing the Dossier ID and a reason; it explicitly does NOT permanently destroy the dossier — it archives it to a recoverable Trash (restorable with undo), and the action is recorded on the append-only audit trail.

"Portfolio" (under an "Operations" eyebrow) shows "Every product dossier in your organisation — module progress, filing gate and fee status at a glance," plus "Every change on this page is captured in the dossier's append-only audit trail — actor and workspace stamped, sequence-numbered, exportable for inspections (open a dossier → Audit)." A per-client / sponsor scope selector is the first control, and the full dossier grid can be shown or hidden. Rows load fee state (paid, waived, or an amount due in CAD) and live PM(NOC) clocks — days remaining on a served NOA or a running stay. A button offers "Export client status report (CSV)" with columns including filing_gate and fee_status.

"Account & security" shows "Who you are here" — Signed in as (your email), Workspace "(from the account record — every dossier, document and filing here is isolated to this workspace)," Role, and an Identity row that reads either "SSO-verified ✓" (an IdP-authenticated principal) or "Recorded email" (password sign-in). "Multi-factor authentication" offers "Set up authenticator app →"; enrollment shows a secret with "Copy setup link," then "enter the current 6-digit code to confirm" and "Turn on MFA →", noting "Nothing is enforced until this code verifies." When on, a chip reads "Enabled ✓". "Password & sessions" states you stay signed in for 12 hours, with the salted-hash and HttpOnly-cookie detail tucked into a "For your IT department" expander. "Deployment & data residency" states "ANDS Studio is self-hosted… Nothing leaves it except the packages you deliberately transmit to Health Canada," "cross-workspace reads are refused at the API, not just hidden in the UI," and that single sign-on via OIDC (OpenID Connect) is available and configured per workspace — while being honest that SAML, automated provisioning (SCIM) and SIEM streaming remain on the roadmap.

"Regulatory reference" (Help) says "The primary Health Canada sources behind everything this app checks and generates… so you can read the rule, not just trust the tool." Link cards cover Canadian Module 1, REP, eCTD guidance, Forms, PM(NOC) Regulations, comparative bioavailability, QOS-CE templates, CESG ("This app prepares and simulates; the gateway account is yours"), fees ("the small-business reduction and first-submission waiver the fees step applies"), and DIN annual obligations ("Annual notification and Right-to-Sell — tracked in Registry"). "How validation works here" lists rule families CA-E-1xxx through CA-E-4xxx and CA-REP-0001 ("filing is blocked while a dossier still uses a placeholder ID"), followed by "The complete rule catalogue," pulled live from the engine with a rule count. "How AI drafting is controlled" states it is opt-in per section (only sections marked "✦AI"), "Nothing is saved until you click Use this draft," every AI-assisted document is "permanently labeled (AI-assisted — review before filing)," and "the human review + e-signature gate still stands between any document and transmission." A closing tip notes dashed-underlined terms reveal plain-language definitions on hover.
